correctness.rationale: Fixing one source and image leaves the two possible dihedral orientations. A second source fixes the orientation except at an antipode, and a third distinct source always fixes it. A restriction is nilpotent exactly when it omits some vertex from every ambient permutation cycle. This gives the stated rotation and reflection terms; remove 2n−1 surplus empty restrictions, one surplus restriction per nonidentity singleton map, and n(n−2)/2 for even n from bijections between distinct antipodal pairs. The rotation terms reach rank n−1 only at order n, with coefficient nφ(n); reflections cannot reach it for n≥3. At each nonantipodal distance, the 2n² rank-two maps lose 2n for equal domain and image and 2n for a fixed vertex in a distinct overlapping pair; the antipodal distance contributes n(n−2)/2. For density, orders d≤ceil(2 log₂ n) cost O(log² n) rotations, and the relative deficit 1−(1−2⁻ᵈ)^(n/d) for any larger order is at most 1/n. Reflections contribute at most n·3^(n/2); the duplicate correction and the denominator's departure from 2n·2ⁿ are O(n²). Independent enumeration of partial bijections directly by distance and iterated image gave all rank coefficients for n=3–7 without assuming dihedral extension.

evidence: Substitute z=1 in the earlier formula; the rotation terms normalized by 2ⁿ are (1−2⁻ᵈ)^(n/d). Splitting the totient sum at twice log₂ n and using Bernoulli's inequality gives exactly the stated O(log² n/n) density error. Substituting n=3 yields 1+6z+6z².
